verdict.summary: You can create a Google OAuth client and connect your own Gmail account in minutes. Public use with any read/modify Gmail scope (including Composio's default https://mail.google.com/) needs Google verification plus a yearly third-party CASA security assessment, which takes weeks to months. An app that only sends mail (gmail.send, a sensitive scope) still needs verification but avoids CASA.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 30-60 min for Gates 1-2; several days of work for Gate 3 (domain verification, privacy policy, demo video, CASA questionnaire and fixes)
verdict.approval_wait: Several weeks for restricted scopes (community reports say 4-6 weeks), and Google says some verification can take several months; CASA is extra

gates.name: Testing publishing status (your own account)
gates.unlocks: You connect your own Google account through your own OAuth client, with any Gmail scope, no review.
limits: Users see the unverified-app screen when sensitive or restricted scopes are requested
Refresh tokens reportedly expire after about 7 days in External + Testing status (community report, not confirmed by Google)

gates.name: Testing status / unverified app with known test users
gates.unlocks: A small group of known users (teammates, testers) can authorize the app without verification. Google exempts development/testing projects and personal use by a few known users from verification.
limits: An unverified app is capped at 100 new users in total once it shows the unverified-app screen
Unverified-app warning screen shown to every user
Refresh tokens reportedly expire about 7 days after issue in Testing status (community)
Reportedly a limit of 100 live refresh tokens per Google Account per client ID (community)

gates.name: Production status + verified app (brand verification, data access review, CASA for restricted scopes)
gates.unlocks: Anyone with a Google account can connect, with no unverified-app screen and no 100-user cap. Refresh tokens stay valid until revoked.
limits: Restricted scopes (gmail.readonly, gmail.modify, gmail.compose, mail.google.com, etc.) need a yearly security assessment by a Google-approved third party (CASA) if data is stored on or sent through servers
Adding redirect URIs/JS origins, changing the product name, or adding scopes may mean verifying again

steps.title: Sign in and create a Google Cloud project
steps.detail: Sign in to the Google Cloud console with a Google account and create a new project for this integration. The Credentials page sits behind a Google sign-in.

steps.title: Enable the Gmail API
steps.detail: In the project, open APIs & Services > Library, search for Gmail API and click Enable.

steps.title: Pick the smallest Gmail scope set
steps.detail: List the Gmail actions your agent actually needs and map them to the smallest scopes. Send-only apps should use gmail.send (sensitive) and not mail.google.com or gmail.readonly/modify (restricted). Composio's default set includes https://mail.google.com/, which brings in the full restricted-scope review.
gotchas: Google says to request mail.google.com only if you need to immediately and permanently delete messages.
Read plus send spans both review tiers (sensitive and restricted).

steps.title: Configure the OAuth consent screen
steps.detail: Under APIs & Services, set up the OAuth consent screen: user type External, app name, user support email, developer contact email and a privacy policy URL. Add exactly the scopes from the previous step. Leave publishing status as Testing for now.
gotchas: The scopes requested in code (your Composio auth config) must match the consent screen, or users see the unverified-app screen.
Google's Trust & Safety team sends review questions to the support and developer contact emails, so use inboxes someone checks.

steps.title: Create the OAuth client ID
steps.detail: Go to Credentials > Create credentials > OAuth client ID, choose application type Web application, and add the redirect URI. Copy the client ID and client secret.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Set the final redirect URI now. Adding redirect URIs after verification means verifying again.

steps.title: Add the credentials to Composio and test-connect your account
steps.detail: Create a Gmail auth config in Composio that uses your own client ID and secret and the same scopes as the consent screen, then run a test authorization with your own Google account. Make sure offline access is requested so a refresh token is issued and stored.
gotchas: If you get no refresh token on re-consent, force the consent prompt (approval_prompt=force / prompt=consent).

steps.title: Invite test users
steps.detail: While in Testing, let a small number of known testers authorize the app. They will see the unverified-app screen. Expect to reconnect about weekly if refresh tokens expire after 7 days in Testing.
gotchas: Hard cap of 100 new users in total for an unverified app.
The 7-day token expiry comes from community reports, not from Google.

steps.title: Publish a home page and privacy policy on a verified domain
steps.detail: Draft a public home page that clearly describes the app, and a privacy policy on the same domain that explains how Google user data is used, stored and shared. Then verify domain ownership in Google Search Console (a project owner or editor must do the Search Console verification) and add it as an authorized domain.
gotchas: A Play Store listing or Facebook page is not accepted as a home page.
Search Console verification must be done by a project owner or editor (a 'you' action).

steps.title: Record the demo video
steps.detail: Record the full grant flow: the consent screen showing the app name and client ID, then how each sensitive or restricted scope is used in the app. Upload it to YouTube Studio with Visibility set to Unlisted.

steps.title: Switch to Production and submit for verification
steps.detail: In the OAuth consent screen, change the publishing status to Production and submit for verification with your scope justifications and the video link. An agent can draft the justification text, but the status switch can only be made in the console UI.

steps.title: Wait for brand verification and data access review
steps.detail: Google first runs brand verification (domains, branding), then reviews data access for sensitive/restricted scopes. Answer Trust & Safety emails quickly.
gotchas: Compliant brand verification results are valid for only 7 days, so submit promptly after passing.

steps.title: Complete the CASA security assessment (restricted scopes only)
steps.detail: If you request restricted Gmail scopes and store or send that data through servers, get a security assessment from a Google-approved App Defense Alliance lab under the CASA framework. Budget time for fixes. Cost is unclear, with community estimates from about $500 to $75,000.
steps.est_time: Days of work plus lab turnaround

steps.title: Keep verification current
steps.detail: Renew the CASA assessment every year, and avoid changing the client, product name, redirect URIs or scopes without planning for re-verification.
gotchas: Community reports say a missed renewal can lead to production access being revoked.

requirements.item: Google account with access to the Cloud console
requirements.detail: Needed to create the project and OAuth client.

requirements.item: Privacy policy URL on the consent screen
requirements.detail: Required on the consent screen. For verification it must be on the same domain as the home page and must disclose how Google user data is used, stored and shared.

requirements.item: Public home page relevant to the app
requirements.detail: Must be publicly accessible. App-store or social pages are not accepted.

requirements.item: Authorized domains verified in Search Console
requirements.detail: Checked during brand verification, and verified by a project owner or editor.
Shows the consent flow with app name and client ID, and how each sensitive/restricted scope is used.
Required for restricted scopes when data is stored on or sent through servers.

requirements.item: Compliance with Google Workspace user data policy
requirements.detail: This is the policy that governs Gmail API access.

scopes.effect: Full mailbox access, and in Composio's default set. Triggers restricted-scope verification and CASA. Google says to use it only when you need immediate permanent deletion.
Restricted-scope verification plus a yearly CASA assessment if data passes through servers.
Restricted, and for admin use only.
Needs OAuth app verification but not CASA. The best choice for send-only agents.
Profile scopes in Composio's default set. No extra Gmail review is documented in the findings.

blockers.symptom: Users see 'Google hasn't verified this app' and new sign-ups stop after 100 users
blockers.cause: The app is unverified and requests sensitive/restricted scopes.
blockers.fix: Complete verification (Gate 3). Also make sure the scopes in code match the consent screen.

blockers.symptom: Connections break with invalid_grant about a week after authorizing
blockers.cause: Reported 7-day refresh-token expiry for External apps in Testing status.
blockers.fix: Move to Production status (and verify). Until then, reconnect test users.

blockers.symptom: Verification required again after a small config change
blockers.cause: Adding redirect URIs/JS origins, renaming the product, changing the client or adding scopes after verification.
blockers.fix: Lock the redirect URI, name and scope list before submitting.

blockers.symptom: Verification blocked pending a security assessment
blockers.cause: Restricted Gmail scopes with data stored on or sent through servers need CASA.
blockers.fix: Narrow to sensitive scopes such as gmail.send if possible. Otherwise engage an App Defense Alliance-approved lab.

blockers.symptom: Older connections for one user stop working
blockers.cause: Reported limit of 100 live refresh tokens per Google Account per client ID.
blockers.fix: Reuse stored refresh tokens and don't re-authorize repeatedly.

composio.note: Start on Composio's managed Gmail OAuth to prototype without a Google app. Switch to your own Google OAuth client when you need your own branding on the consent screen or a public launch under your own verification. Composio's default scopes include the restricted https://mail.google.com/ scope, so if you copy them, plan for restricted-scope verification and CASA. Trim to the smallest scopes you need (e.g. gmail.send only) to lower the review burden.

evidence.claim: Composio's default Gmail scope set includes the full-access https://mail.google.com/ scope alongside profile, email and contacts scopes.
Google's OpenID discovery document advertises S256 and plain PKCE methods.
Google's authorize endpoint rejects an unknown client_id, so a real OAuth client ID must be registered.

open_questions: Redirect URI rules for Google web clients (exact match, localhost, limits) were not verified from an official Google page.
PKCE support for the Gmail web-server flow was inferred only from the OIDC discovery document.
Refresh-token lifetime details (7-day Testing expiry, 100 tokens per client, inactivity expiry) come only from community sources.
Verification timelines are not fixed: Google says 'several weeks' to 'several months'. 4-6 weeks is a community estimate.
CASA cost is unknown, with community estimates ranging from about $500/year to $15,000-75,000.
Whether Composio's managed Google OAuth client is verified and CASA-assessed was not checked.
Whether a personal Gmail account (no Workspace org) can create an External consent screen without issues was not confirmed. The Internal user type requires Workspace (community only).
The exact console steps for adding test users to an allowlist were not covered by the findings.
